title: feat(runtime,cli)!: os serve refuses a v17-shape database until the organization-ownership ceremony has verified it (ADR-0131 D10 item 5, C7b S5)
body:
Fixes #23429 · Part of #15211
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

## What changed

The v18 boot refusal (ADR-0131 D10 item 5; ruling 6163114098, Q3 → A).

- **`OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin`** (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`). At `kernel:ready` it asks one question: does a table whose object declares **no** organization column (`systemFields.tenant: false`, no declared `organization_id`) still carry a **physical** `organization_id`? Schema sync only adds columns, so on a database a v17 runtime created the answer stays yes until the ceremony's column-drops step runs. If the answer is yes, the guard reads the ceremony's `sys_migration` marker `adr-0131-organization-ownership`. Unless that marker is verified, it throws `OrganizationOwnershipBootRefusal` (code `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_REQUIRED`). The refusal names the tables and `os migrate organization-ownership`, and it stops `bootstrap()` before `kernel:listening` opens the socket.
  - A fresh database boots: no table it creates carries a retired column.
  - A database whose ceremony verified boots, whatever its columns.
  - A column read that fails is refused, never taken for a migrated database.
  - ⛔ There is no escape hatch: no variable and no flag skips the check (D10 verbatim).
  - A driver with no physical columns (memory, MongoDB) is not checked.
- **Composed by `os serve` only** (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`), beside `MigrationRecoveryPlugin`. It is never in `createStandaloneStack` or `data-migration-plugins.ts`: those are the CLI data and schema boots, the ceremony's own boot among them, and a guard there would refuse the one command that clears it.
- **`ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_ID`** moves to `@objectstack/spec/system` (`migration.zod.ts`) so that the runtime and the ceremony read one constant. The ceremony re-exports it.
- **The error code** is registered in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` under `@objectstack/runtime`. No door answers it: the refusal is thrown before any request is served. The generated api surface, export origins and error-code docs are regenerated.
- **The changeset**: BREAKING. Its ADR-0087 marker is `already-registered`, naming the step-18 column-retired entries of the tables it reads. The metadata family's four entries land with S2.

## Where the refusal sits, and why it is its own plugin

The card names the `kernel:ready` reader shape of `migration-recovery-plugin.ts`, refusing where that plugin warns. The guard takes that shape: the same hook, the same engine reads, and the same "inert without an engine" rule. It is a sibling plugin rather than code inside `MigrationRecoveryPlugin` for one reason: `MigrationRecoveryPlugin` is also composed by the CLI data-migration boot (`packages/cli/src/utils/data-migration-plugins.ts`), the boot the ceremony runs on. A refusal there would refuse the ceremony itself.

## Landing

- This PR lands **together with S2** (the `sys_metadata` family's no-column schema), and only after #15211's S1 (#23452) is on `main` (6163669810).
- S5 cannot land before S2. On today's `main` the family still declares its column, so the guard would not judge the family at all. S2 makes the family `tenant: false`, and only then does the guard cover it.

## Pins

- `organization-ownership-boot-guard.test.ts`: the unit pins over a real SQLite database.
  - ⭐ a v17-shape database is refused, naming the command and every table;
  - an unverified marker is refused;
  - ⭐ a verified marker boots;
  - ⭐ a migrated database (the columns dropped) boots;
  - ⭐ a fresh database boots;
  - a failed read is refused;
  - a column-less driver is inert;
  - the plugin refuses at `kernel:ready`;
  - no environment variable stands the refusal down.
- `organization-ownership-boot-guard.kernel.test.ts` (new): the same verdicts on a **real `ObjectKernel`** (SQL driver, ObjectQL, platform objects, the guard).
  - ⭐ a v17-shape database stops `bootstrap()` with the refusal, and the kernel never reaches `running`;
  - ⭐ the same database with its marker verified boots;
  - an unverified marker is refused;
  - ⭐ a fresh database boots.

The kernel pin exists because the unit pins call the hook by hand, and no unit pin proved that the throw stops a real boot.

**Added after the first report** (os-dev-report 6168648434):
- **`organization-ownership-boot-refusal-order.dogfood.test.ts`**, an end-to-end pin of the upgrade order. It checks five things in turn:
  - a v17-shape file database is refused, naming the command;
  - the refused boot has **already** added `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`, because the refusal fires at `kernel:ready`, after every plugin's `start()` and its additive schema sync;
  - the real CLI `os migrate organization-ownership --apply --backup-taken` completes with no boot in between;
  - the ceremony verifies its marker;
  - the next boot succeeds.

  So no deadlock is possible. **The pin is green only beside S2:** it was 4/4 on a scratch merge of S5 + S2, and again of S5 + S2 + S3, and red on S5 alone by design, because the family still declares its column there. Dogfood runs on `main`'s full battery, not on PR CI, and S5 lands only with S2.
- **A real guard defect, fixed:** the guard read only the driver's `config.client`. A served file database runs on `SqliteWasmDriver`, whose client is a dialect class, so the guard was inert on the default SQLite driver. It now reads `SqlDriver.dialectName`, falling back to the client string, with a unit pin.
- The dogfood package gains an `@objectstack/runtime` dependency, and an anchored source alias for it in its `vitest.config.ts` (`check:test-source-alias`).

## Verification

**Latest head `e39386f2cd`:** the guard unit and kernel pins pass, 14 tests. Runtime and dogfood typecheck exit 0. PR CI is green, 37 of 37 with 5 skipped. The first round follows, all on head `540c5b3c` of this branch (`origin/main` merged once at `24f4483d` before work).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 378 files, 6,276 passed, 19 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: 4,278 passed, 29 skipped. Two files needed a built `cli` (`published-subpath-console.pin`, `published-subpath-hook-body.pin`). After `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` they pass, 29 tests. The `integration` layer is left to CI.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix`: three artifacts were stale (api-surface, export-origins, docs) and are regenerated. `vitest run src/api/error-code-ledger.test.ts`: 21 passed.
- **Ablation**, one-shot, with `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The guard's `if (tables.length === 0) return;` was replaced by an unconditional return. The kernel pin went red as predicted: the two refusal cases failed and the two boot cases stayed green. The file was restored, and its blob equals `HEAD` (`git diff HEAD` empty).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 116 families, and all 116 ran (`--ran` reconciles: 0 unrun). 109 exited 0. Seven are NOT MEASURED, because they refused on a local prerequisite before reading anything; CI runs them:
  - `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`: the shallow clone;
  - `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity` and `check:type-check-debt`: unbuilt packages.
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`: the changeset carries its disposition.
